tldr: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra on Sep 11, and Simon Willison's Sep 12 hands-on showed a 27-minute unattended run. Perplexity's Sep 14 case study then showed production monitoring delegated with far fewer check-ins, before OpenAI rated Astra Critical for cybersecurity on Sep 17 after testers found real 0-days in a browser and an OS kernel.
whats_new: Basis became the fourth customer case study since the Critical cybersecurity rating, reporting Astra finished a 50-tab tax workbook 2x faster than GPT-5.6 Sol; still no visible new access limits.
why_it_matters: A model good enough to find real 0-days in a browser and a kernel is also good enough to weaponize them, so expect OpenAI to tighten access, logging, or usage terms around Astra's offensive-security capability rather than treating a growing run of adoption case studies as the full picture.

status.detail: Production adoption was accelerating on trust and reduced oversight when OpenAI's Preparedness Framework classified Astra as Critical-risk for cybersecurity after it found real, previously unknown vulnerabilities; customer case studies have continued since (Higgsfield, Harvey, Basis).

beats.headline: A 27-minute unattended run backs the long-running-task claim
beats.summary: Simon Willison had ChatGPT Work with Astra plan 5K and 10K running routes from OSM data; it ran unattended for 27 minutes and returned two accurate routes.

beats.headline: Customer trust escalates from self-testing to full delegation
beats.summary: Cognition's Devin tested its own generated code with Astra and Hex turned its analysis into shareable reports the same week; Perplexity went further, delegating production monitoring and code changes with far fewer human check-ins.

beats.headline: OpenAI classifies Astra Critical for cybersecurity after it finds real 0-days
beats.summary: Expert-led Preparedness Framework testing found previously unknown vulnerabilities in a browser and an OS kernel, making Astra the first model OpenAI has rated Critical on that axis.

beats.headline: Customer adoption keeps accelerating despite the Critical rating
beats.summary: Higgsfield shipped video ad-creation features four days after the classification, Harvey improved legal drafts, and Basis finished a 50-tab tax workbook 2x faster than GPT-5.6 Sol (a vendor-reported comparison) -- no visible new restrictions.

open_questions: Do Astra's launch-week coding and computer-use gains hold up in independent, third-party benchmarks rather than vendor case studies?
Does Perplexity's reduced check-in frequency reflect genuine reliability, or looser production guardrails that haven't yet been tested by a failure?

Nearly two weeks past the Critical classification and four case studies in, has OpenAI added any new access restrictions, usage logging, or eval requirements for API customers, and were the browser/kernel vulnerabilities disclosed and patched?
take_for_builders: If you're using Astra for offensive-security testing or automated vulnerability discovery, expect OpenAI to add usage restrictions or heavier logging now that it's rated Critical -- four vendor case studies since the rating haven't triggered a visible change yet, but check your API terms before the next audit cycle, not after.
